### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Springer Nature (publisher-wide policy, applies to Topoi as no journal-specific override found): generative AI/LLMs cannot be listed as author. Use of an LLM in manuscript preparation must be disclosed in the Methods section (or a suitable alternative section if no Methods section exists); AI-assisted copy-editing is exempt from disclosure. AI-generated images/videos are not permitted for publication. This is Springer's group-wide policy referenced generically from Topoi's submission-guidelines page (which points authors to Springer's generative-AI policy) — I could not fetch the Topoi-specific submission-guidelines page directly (paywall/login redirect on link.springer.com), so this is inferred from the general Springer policy plus search-engine-cached summaries of that guidelines page, not a first-hand read of Topoi's own page. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.springernature.com/gp/authors/generative-ai-policy |

| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | *(pending — no evidentiary basis collected; would require reading a sample of recent articles)* |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | *(pending)* |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | *(pending)* |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Topoi publishes single-theme special issues, usually with a guest editor who is a domain expert; recent/current issues and CFPs (2025-2026) span core analytic-continental philosophy topics (implicit bias, moral exemplarism, the principle of charity in argumentation/interpretation, rule-following, slurring terms across languages, linguistic derogation) alongside an explicit, self-described 'experiment' issue on 'Technology, Nature, and Wellbeing in Contemporary Societies' that deliberately accepted papers authored mostly by non-philosophers (neuroscience, experimental psychology, neurology, informatics, biomedical engineering, social neuroscience) and guest-edited by non-philosophers. Editor Fabio Paglieri (Daily Nous, 2025-04-29) stated the journal has 'always been open to all philosophical schools and areas' and is 'quite liberal in integrating contributions from other disciplines if deemed philosophically relevant,' but characterized the fully-interdisciplinary special issue as 'an exception' rather than the new norm going forward.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** analytic philosophy argumentation/conceptual analysis, philosophy of science, philosophy of technology, epistemology, philosophy of language / linguistics-adjacent argument analysis, empirical/interdisciplinary papers (neuroscience, psychology, biomedical/informatics) — only within specific guest-edited special issues explicitly soliciting them, e.g. the Technology/Nature/Wellbeing collection
